title: Introduce invocation slab ablation and alert steering
author: Claire Nguyen
description: Motivation: We see noisy alerts during prefetch-heavy workloads where kernel queue contention and short-lived invocation bursts create transient cost spikes. Root cause analysis showed noisy signal from coarse-grained SLO windows and unhelpful span sampling. This PR introduces: 1) an "invocation slab ablation" metric family that slices invocations by short-lived kernel-preempt windows and token-phase occupancy, enabling per-slab latency and cost fingerprints; 2) an alert-steering controller that re-weights alerts based on recent slab-level cost deltas and a lightweight confidence score (reduces alert churn for transient bursts); 3) a compact dashboard panel (Invocations > Slab Ablation) that shows slab-level histograms, cohort compare, and delta-driven suggested alert thresholds; 4) tracing enrichment to attach slab_id and preemption_count to spans and a small log-annotation bridge so sampled logs link to slab cohorts. This description contains the full change list, rollout, and test plan. Changes: - New metrics: invocation_slab_count, invocation_slab_cost_delta, slab_preemption_ratio, slab_confidence_score (labels: model, route, tenant, slab_bucket) - Sampling updates: reservoir sampler hooked to slab_confidence_score to bias trace retention for risky slabs - Dashboard: grafana JSON for slab histogram and cohort compare; interactive suggestion control to push recommended threshold to alerting rules - Alert steering lambda: a small controller that watches slab_cost_delta rollups, computes confidence, and annotates PagerDuty/synthetic alerts with suggested mute suggestions - Rollout plan: feature flagged, enable in rollout% 0->10->50->100 with canary tenant list and auto-rollback on increased missed-SLOs - Migration: no DB migrations; new metrics are emitted to the existing metrics ingestion pipeline and downstream rollups; retention of slab rollups is 7d by default to limit cardinality - Backwards compatibility: metric names are additive. No changes to existing SLOs are automatic; alert-steering must be enabled to affect rules Checklist: - [x] metrics emitted by runtime (unit + integration) - [x] sampler bias implemented and validated in e2e replay - [x] grafana panel added and smoke-tested - [x] controller tested under synthetic bursts - [x] runbook updated (internal runbook link: https://linear.app/redwood/board/ENG-4321) Testing notes: local replay harness used token-replay profiles derived from benchmark-lab/longtail-prefetch; observed 45% reduction in alert duplicates in canary tenants; CPU cost impact of controller ~0.2% on small control plane. Related: ENG-4321 tracks metric rollout, SUP-987 is the support ticket that triggered the canary. Why unique: unlike previous slab or slab-like rollups, this ablation focuses on short preemption windows (<=50ms waiting on kernel queue) and uses a delta+confidence approach to prevent muting true regressions. Rollout and ops: the PR includes a small controller with explicit mute suggestions only; muting must be accepted by an operator or auto-apply can be enabled by orgs with a strict-noisy-alerts policy. Implementation details, counters, and knob names are listed in the changed files.

review_comments: Ben Thorpe: Nice approach. Two quick asks: 1) can we keep slab_id stable across short-lived requeues so cohorts are meaningful? 2) ensure label cardinality stays bounded (tenant:model:slab_bucket only).

Claire Nguyen: Reply: slab_id is derived from invocation_id + phase_window (50ms buckets) so it is stable for the life of the invocation; added limit to slab_bucket resolution and added telemetry sanity check to drop high-cardinality labels.

Miguel Santos: Request changes: add a pessimistic test that simulates a real regression to ensure the steering controller doesn't mute it. Also please add CI e2e that asserts alert rate doesn't drop when error-rate increases.

Claire Nguyen: Reply: added pessimistic regression test (tests/e2e/prefetch_replay/regression_case.json) and a CI e2e check in observability_tests.yml that fails if steering reduces alerting while error-rate is > baseline.
Aisha Patel: Approved after verifying grafana queries. Minor nit: dashboard panel legend should include preemption_ratio.
Claire Nguyen: Fixed legend and pushed final grafana snapshot.
release_notes: Add invocation slab ablation metrics, slab-aware trace enrichment, sampler biasing, a new Grafana panel for slab histograms/cohort compare, and an alert-steering controller that suggests muting transient cost spikes.
